observations.statement: The appellate record makes automated fraud-probability outputs and account removals addressable.
The public account records that affected drivers were not heard before significant decisions.
The court required information sufficient to understand and contest relevant automated decisions.
Collective representation helped bring the information and explanation dispute into court.
The public record does not disclose a complete worker-level restoration or compensation ledger.
No same-chain model, threshold, workflow revision, independent implementation audit, or survivor-bias reconciliation is recovered.

open_questions: Was the correction implemented at the operative system boundary?
Were affected records, access, pay, duties, or accounts restored?
Was implementation independently verified after the deadline?
Did exits, silence, deterrence, overturns, restoration, and compensation enter later validation?
title: Uber and Ola: explanation orders versus restoration and model revision
